“the stakes for our company has never been higher” >>> “the stakes for our company have never been higher”
“federal goverment” >>> “federal government”
“matters more then ever” >>> “matters more than ever”
“has three cosponsors on the committee, Senators Okafor and Lindqvist” >>> [CHECK: Three cosponsors are claimed, but only two are named.]
“it's definitions are broad” >>> “its definitions are broad”
“its central principal” >>> “its central principle”
“In brief, the bill:” >>> “In brief:”
“enforcment regime” >>> “enforcement regime”
“directly effect every company” >>> “directly affect every company”
“Senator Whitfield (R-OK)” >>> [CHECK: Whitfield is identified as R-OH earlier.]
“narrows the registry in Section 5” >>> “narrows the registry in Section 4”
“keeps the $10 million daily civil penalty in Section 5” >>> [CHECK: The earlier summary specifies $1 million per day; confirm the amount and whether the amendment keeps or changes it.]
“who's support” >>> “whose support”
“the amendment's changes is modest” >>> “the amendment's changes are modest”
“of the committees 28 members” >>> “of the committee's 28 members”
“13 are yes or leaning yes, 10 are no or leaning no, and 6 are undecided” >>> [CHECK: These counts total 29, but the committee is said to have 28 members.]
“The undecided senators are Chen, Ellis, Alvarez, Pike, and Barlow.” >>> [CHECK: Five senators are listed, but the preceding sentence says six are undecided.]
“Thursday, October 14” >>> “Thursday, October 15”
“a seperate interview” >>> “a separate interview”
“Senator Kowalski, who withdrew his cosponsorship on October 2, has not committed to voting no; in a seperate interview, Senator Ames said he has not made a final decision either.” >>> [CHECK: Neither Kowalski nor Ames appears in the undecided list. Confirm whether they are classified as leaning or should be included.]
“The list of undecided senators, along with their staff contacts, are attached.” >>> “The list of undecided senators, along with their staff contacts, is attached.”
“Commerce Commitee markup” >>> “Commerce Committee markup”
“as soon as the week November 16” >>> “as soon as the week of November 16”
“occured on September 30” >>> “occurred on September 30”
“The committee's hearing on the risks of advanced AI occured on September 30” >>> [CHECK: The votes section references a September 23 hearing. Confirm whether these are separate hearings or inconsistent dates.]
“the treaty negotiations required by Section 6 would have to conclude within two years” >>> [CHECK: The Section 6 summary specifies 18 months, not two years.]
“a close compliment to S. 2817” >>> “a close complement to S. 2817”
“with the the offices” >>> “with the offices”
“call there senators” >>> “call their senators”
“should recieve updated talking points” >>> “should receive updated talking points”
“Each of our five regional policy leads” >>> [CHECK: The preceding paragraph says there are six regional policy leads.]
